assets.scope: Immovable jelly family (jelly.lua); native occurrence spans Maze, Norgos, Sandworm Lair and flooded Trollmire among 7 areas per docs/expansion-plan-20260928/PLAN.md; exact identity only, no subtype-wide substitution

references.note: Approved amorphous-subject style anchor: reuse its steep overhead three-quarter camera, matte sculpted miniature finish, thin charcoal-brown physical disc and muted bronze-grey bevel, and how a rounded immovable ground body fills the disc without legs or a facing direction. Do not copy its species, colour or lobed rosette shape.
Native green jelly colour only. Ignore the native flat blob rendering and its camera; our version is a sculpted three-dimensional mound.
Existing mapped brown mold: its concentric hard-shell growth rings are already taken. Green jelly must read as a soft translucent dome with suspended debris, not a hard ringed shell.

prompt_fields.subject: One green jelly: a smooth, semi-translucent rounded dome sitting low and wide, its base spreading into an uneven ring where it meets the disc. A scatter of small dark debris chunks and a few round bubbles are visible suspended just under the glassy surface, denser near the centre. The surface has one broad soft highlight across the upper-left dome consistent with the lighting, and gentle rounded ripples break the otherwise smooth profile.
prompt_fields.contrast: The other three jellies in this set are the same stationary mound body plan and must not be told apart by hue alone. Give green jelly the most translucent, glassy surface of the four, with visible suspended debris reading as small darker specks breaking up an otherwise smooth mid-green dome (silhouette: gently rippled dome edge with debris-caused micro-bumps; value: mid-value body with scattered small dark inclusions, unlike the glossy tar sheen of black jelly, the faceted frosted look of white jelly or the blistered surface of yellow jelly).
prompt_fields.composition: One entire stationary mound on one disc, steep overhead three-quarter view, centred with no facing direction (this creature never moves). The body sits low and wide, its base spreading unevenly where it meets the disc; every bump, facet or inclusion stays inside the disc with the outer sixth of the disc radius left as bare base plate. Keep the tallest point of the mound out of the upper-right rank corner and the upper-left interaction corner. No second creature, no puddle trail, no scenery.
prompt_fields.palette: Translucent moss and bottle green with a paler yellow-green lit crown, small charcoal-brown debris specks and pale bubble highlights suspended under the surface, deep olive base shadow. No glow, no poison cloud, no effect, no ground stain.
